newsitem.title: UK: BA Cargo says no move yet on fuel surcharge.
newsitem.headline: BA Cargo says no move yet on fuel surcharge.

text.p: British Airways World Cargo division said no decision has yet been taken on whether or not to introduce a fuel surcharge for cargo traffic.
"The matter is still being discussed and no decision has been taken," a World Cargo spokesman told Reuters.

Earlier on Tuesday, an spokesman for the International Air Transport Association (IATA) in Geneva said the organisation will hold an emergency meeting on November 13 to consider "concerted action" by airlines to counter rising jet fuel costs.
Also on Tuesday, KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV announced a worldwide cargo fuel surcharge of 0.20 guilders per kg with effect from November 1.
It was followed by Swissair with a 10 cents per kg rise in cargo rates from November 15.
On October 25, Lufthansa Cargo said it was introducing a 10 cents per kg worldwide surcharge for cargo but on November 1.
France's national carrier, Air France said it will decide today or Wednesday morning whether to increase cargo tariffs because of the pressure on fuel prices.
Air cargo industry sources in London said they understand that both U.S. and Japanese airlines are now actively considering whether or not to follow the European moves.
"Everyone is talking about it, but it is a question of waiting to see who makes the first move," said a London cargo official for a U.S. airline.
